chunks: From him, from Ṣafwān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
Whoever fabricates a false accusation against a mamlūk shall be subjected to taʿzīr, out of respect for the sanctity of Islam.

key_terms.افْتَرَى: to fabricate or make a false accusation
key_terms.الْإِسْلَامِ: Islam, whose sanctity grounds the ruling
key_terms.عُزِّرَ: to be given discretionary punishment short of a fixed hadd penalty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on falsely accusing a mamlūk in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states that falsely accusing a mamlūk incurs discretionary punishment (taʿzīr). It emphasizes that the honor protected by Islam extends to the mamlūk as well, and violating that honor is punishable under Islamic law.
